system.label: Agent identity and rules
system.text:
You are a senior software engineer on a team that maintains a production Python codebase. You
have been handed one change request. You own it from understanding the requirement to delivering
code that a reviewer can approve and merge.

Your responsibilities

Understand the requirement.
- Read the request as the product team means it, not only its literal words. Work out the inputs,
  the expected outputs, the error cases and the edge cases it implies.
- Where the request is ambiguous, choose the interpretation most consistent with the rest of the
  system and with what users of the feature would expect.

Understand the code before changing it.
- Read the code you are changing and the code it depends on or that depends on it, as far as it is
  available to you. Know what a function does from its code, not only from its name.
- Know who calls what you change. Keep public interfaces, data formats and behaviour that other code
  relies on intact unless the request asks you to change them.

Make the change correctly.
- Correctness comes first: the new behaviour must be right for every input the request implies,
  including empty, missing, zero, negative, very large and malformed values where relevant.
- Handle errors the way the codebase does: fail clearly on invalid input; never silently return
  wrong data.
- Treat money, dates, units and identifiers with care: exact arithmetic where the codebase uses it,
  explicit units, no lossy conversions.
- Don't introduce security problems: validate untrusted input and keep secrets and personal data
  out of logs and output.

Keep the codebase healthy.
- Fit in with the surrounding code: its naming, structure, typing and error handling. A reviewer
  should not be able to tell which lines are new by their style.
- Keep the change as small as the request allows, and complete: every file the change needs, none
  it doesn't. Don't refactor, rename or reformat unrelated code.
- Write code that is simple and readable; add a docstring or comment where intent is not obvious.

Check your work.
- You cannot run the code, so verify it by reading it: trace the main path and each edge case
  through your change, check every import and name you use exists, and check that everything that
  calls the code you changed still works.
- Your change will be applied to the repository and checked by tests you do not see.

What you are given
- <task>: the change request from the product team.
- <context>: material from the repository. How much varies: it may be a single file or much of the
  project. It is what you know about the codebase.

What you can and cannot do
- You cannot run code, and there is no one to ask.
- If tools are provided with this request, you may use them to look at the repository before you
  answer. If no tools are provided, you cannot open files or search: deliver the finished change in
  this reply. Tool calls, plans and requests for more files written as text are not executed, and a
  reply without code counts as no change.
- If something you need is not shown, make the most reasonable assumption consistent with what is
  shown, and implement it.

Output format (strict)
Your reply is the code change itself. Return the complete new contents of every file you create or
modify, each wrapped exactly as:
<file path="PATH">
...full file contents...
</file>
- Replace PATH with the file's real path relative to the repository root, as shown in <context> or
  <task>.
- Always the whole file, never a diff or an excerpt, and no placeholders such as "rest unchanged".
- Files you don't change are left out.
- Return nothing outside the <file> blocks: no explanations, plans or summaries before or after them.

user.text:
Shoppers can add a gift message to an order. Add `gift_message: str = ""` to `Order`. The message
must be printed on the packing slip of the order's first parcel only: carry it through
`split_into_parcels` so that `packing_slip(parcel, weight_g)` can print it. The order
representation the API returns must include it as `gift_message`. Customer invoices must not show
it.

[#2] read_symbol shopkit.orders.fulfillment.split_into_parcels

def split_into_parcels(order: Order, max_items: int = MAX_ITEMS_PER_PARCEL) -> list[Parcel]:
    """One unit per slot, at most `max_items` units per parcel, lines kept together where possible."""
    units = [line.sku for line in order.lines for _ in range(line.qty)]
    parcels = []
    for n, batch in enumerate(chunked(units, max_items), start=1):
        counts = group_by(batch, key=lambda s: s)
        parcels.append(Parcel(order.id, n, [(sku, len(v)) for sku, v in counts.items()]))
    return parcels

[#3] read_symbol shopkit.orders.fulfillment.packing_slip
shopkit/orders/fulfillment.py:38-42  shopkit.orders.fulfillment.packing_slip
def packing_slip(parcel: Parcel, weight_g: int) -> str:
    """Slip packed inside each parcel: order, parcel number, contents and weight."""
    lines = [f"Order {parcel.order_id} - parcel {parcel.number}", f"Weight: {format_weight(weight_g)}"]
    lines += [f"  {qty} x {sku}" for sku, qty in parcel.items]

"""Issue invoices for paid orders and credit notes for refunds, keeping both sequences gap-free."""
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date

from shopkit.customers.models import Address
from shopkit.invoices import credit_notes
from shopkit.invoices.layout import footer, header
from shopkit.invoices.numbering import next_invoice_number
from shopkit.invoices.render import render_invoice_text
from shopkit.orders.models import Order


@dataclass
class IssuedInvoice:
    number: str
    order_id: str
    issued: date
    text: str


@dataclass
class InvoiceRegister:
    invoices: list[IssuedInvoice] = field(default_factory=list)
    credit_notes: list[credit_notes.CreditNote] = field(default_factory=list)

    def last_number(self) -> str | None:
        return self.invoices[-1].number if self.invoices else None

    def issue(self, order: Order, bill_to: Address, issued: date) -> IssuedInvoice:
        if any(i.order_id == order.id for i in self.invoices):
            raise ValueError(f"order {order.id} is already invoiced")
        number = next_invoice_number(self.last_number(), issued.year)
        text = "\n\n".join([header(number, issued, bill_to), render_invoice_text(order), footer()])
        invoice = IssuedInvoice(number, order.id, issued, text)
        self.invoices.append(invoice)
        return invoice

    def credit(self, order_id: str, refund_cents: int, currency: str, issued: date,
               reason: str) -> credit_notes.CreditNote:
        invoice = next(i for i in self.invoices if i.order_id == order_id)
        last = self.credit_notes[-1].number if self.credit_notes else None
        note = credit_notes.issue(last, invoice.number, refund_cents, currency, issued, reason)
        self.credit_notes.append(note)
        return note

"""Picking and packing. Builds pick lists for the warehouse and splits orders into parcels."""
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from shopkit.orders.models import Order
from shopkit.shipping.packaging import format_weight
from shopkit.utils.collections import chunked, group_by

MAX_ITEMS_PER_PARCEL = 10


@dataclass
class Parcel:
    order_id: str
    number: int
    items: list[tuple[str, int]] = field(default_factory=list)    # (sku, qty)
    gift_message: str = ""

    @property
    def item_count(self) -> int:
        return sum(q for _, q in self.items)


def pick_list(orders: list[Order]) -> list[tuple[str, int]]:
    """Total quantity per SKU across orders, sorted by SKU (the order pickers walk the aisles)."""
    by_sku = group_by((line for o in orders for line in o.lines), key=lambda l: l.sku)
    return sorted((sku, sum(l.qty for l in lines)) for sku, lines in by_sku.items())


def split_into_parcels(order: Order, max_items: int = MAX_ITEMS_PER_PARCEL) -> list[Parcel]:
    """One unit per slot, at most `max_items` units per parcel, lines kept together where possible.

    The gift message is carried onto the first parcel only, so the packing slip of the other
    parcels in a multi-parcel shipment doesn't repeat it.
    """
    units = [line.sku for line in order.lines for _ in range(line.qty)]
    parcels = []
    for n, batch in enumerate(chunked(units, max_items), start=1):
        counts = group_by(batch, key=lambda s: s)
        parcels.append(Parcel(order.id, n, [(sku, len(v)) for sku, v in counts.items()],
                              gift_message=order.gift_message if n == 1 else ""))
    return parcels


def packing_slip(parcel: Parcel, weight_g: int) -> str:
    """Slip packed inside each parcel: order, parcel number, contents, weight and gift message."""
    lines = [f"Order {parcel.order_id} - parcel {parcel.number}", f"Weight: {format_weight(weight_g)}"]
    lines += [f"  {qty} x {sku}" for sku, qty in parcel.items]
    if parcel.gift_message:
        lines.append(f"Gift message: {parcel.gift_message}")
    return "\n".join(lines)
